about: Resilio Versio demo clips, round 2. Each clip is a pair rendered by the project's Renderer from one dry source: BLEND fully left (the clean passthrough) and BLEND fully right (the wet), with the same gain, so the page's BLEND fader mixes them like the knob. Parts are written and sequenced in code from CC0 samples: Virtuosity Drums (Versilian Studios and Karoryfer), the Baby Blue bass and Emilyguitar (Karoryfer), the FreePats Drawbar Organ, the VSCO 2 CE trombone and VCSL vibraphone, TX81Z clav, Dan Tranh and bongos (Versilian Studios), and a TR-808 cowbell (Michael Fischer, via TidalCycles); the siren is synthesised. MP3 160 kbps, 48 kHz stereo; the mix at each clip's BLEND is about -20.5 LUFS (the drum-heavy clips about 1.4 dB lower), peaks at or below -1 dBTP.

clips.title: Tubby throw and sweep
clips.caption: A one-drop in A minor. The rimshot on bars 2, 4 and 6 is thrown into the springs, then the last two bars go in whole while TONE rides up to the “Big Knob” and back down the tail.
clips.transcript: A reggae one-drop at 76 bpm. Swung hi-hats with open-hat lifts, kick and rimshot together on beat three, soft cross-stick ghosts, and a roots bassline that leaves gaps. On bars two, four and six the rimshot alone splashes into the springs and rings on. Then the whole band goes into the springs for the last two bars, and the reverb turns thin and bright like a telephone, holds there, and warms up again as the long tail fades.
clips.note: Drums: Virtuosity Drums by Versilian Studios and Karoryfer (CC0). Bass: Baby Blue by Karoryfer (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Organ bubble into echo
clips.caption: The reggae organ bubble and guitar chops into the tape echo, clocked to the tempo on dotted eighths. In the last bar the band stops and the echo answers.
clips.transcript: An organ plays the reggae bubble, a shuffling two-handed pattern of short chords, over A minor seven and D nine at 76 bpm. A clean guitar chops on beats two and four. Each chord comes back as dotted-eighth repeats that fall between the beats and thicken the shuffle. In the last bar the organ stops after two beats and the final guitar chops repeat on their own and fade.
clips.note: Organ: FreePats Drawbar Organ (CC0). Guitar: Emilyguitar by Karoryfer (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Trombone dub
clips.caption: A trombone calls and the echo answers in the gaps. On the last phrase DECAY comes up so the repeats pile up, then a turn of TENSION bends the tape.
clips.transcript: A lone trombone plays three short phrases in A minor at 74 bpm, leaving a bar of space after each. The echo fills the space with a few dotted-eighth repeats. On the last phrase the repeats grow longer and louder and keep going after the horn stops. Near the end the repeats swoop up in pitch as the delay time shortens, then fade.
clips.note: Trombone: VSCO 2 CE by Versilian Studios (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Chord stab into the bed
clips.caption: Dub techno in F minor. Short minor-ninth stabs feed a held spring bed that ducks under each kick, with WOBBLE far left for a seasick tape warble. DECAY comes down at the end to let it go.
clips.transcript: A four-on-the-floor kick at 120 bpm with a quiet offbeat hi-hat, and short, syncopated F minor ninth chord stabs on a bright FM keyboard. The springs hold every stab as a continuous wash that dips with each kick and swells between them. After the last stab the wash hangs on for two seconds, then fades away. The bed wavers in pitch the whole time, like a badly worn tape.
clips.note: Clavisynth by Versilian Studios (CC0). Kick and hat: Virtuosity Drums by Versilian Studios and Karoryfer (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Echo chord
clips.caption: One chord every two bars into the tape echo on dotted eighths. TONE rides from warm and dark all the way up to a thin telephone ring, then back down, the classic dub techno filter move.
clips.transcript: A single F minor ninth stab every two bars at 120 bpm, sometimes with a softer second stab pushed just after it. Each stab repeats as a trail of dotted-eighth echoes that fall across the beat. Over the clip the repeats slowly brighten, then darken again.
clips.note: Clavisynth by Versilian Studios (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Vibes in the springs
clips.caption: Slow minor-ninth chords on soft vibraphone, with a warm tail and a little tape drift.
clips.transcript: A vibraphone plays gently rolled chords in D minor, one every few seconds, with a few single notes in between. The springs add a soft, wide bloom behind each chord that drifts very slightly in pitch, and the last chord rings out with a high note on top.
clips.note: VCSL vibraphone by Versilian Studios (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Zither drips
clips.caption: Sparse plucks on a Vietnamese zither, each one dripping into a single spring. Bent notes and a quick run up the strings.
clips.transcript: A Dan Tranh, a plucked Vietnamese zither, plays a slow pentatonic figure with long silences. Every pluck sets off the springy drip of a single reverb tank. Midway there is a fast run up the strings, and two notes are bent upwards after they are plucked.
clips.note: Dan Tranh by Versilian Studios (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Percussion in the springs
clips.caption: Bongos and an 808 cowbell. A few cowbell hits are thrown into the spring and splash, while everything else stays dry.
clips.transcript: Bongos play a busy sixteenth-note pattern of open and muted hits at 118 bpm, with an 808 cowbell on the offbeats and a soft kick from the second bar. Now and then a single cowbell hit bursts into a short, metallic splash of spring reverb while the rest of the groove stays dry.
clips.note: Bongos by Versilian Studios (CC0). TR-808 cowbell from Michael Fischer's 808 set via TidalCycles (CC0). Kick: Virtuosity Drums by Versilian Studios and Karoryfer (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: Guitar warble
clips.caption: A clean guitar letting slow E minor chords ring, with WOBBLE right of noon for a steady tape warble and TENSION loose for a big, slow boing.
clips.transcript: A clean electric guitar picks slow, ringing arpeggios over E minor nine, C major seven, A minor nine and B seven sus at 72 bpm, ending on a soft strum. The spring tail wavers evenly in pitch, a gentle vibrato, and each note blooms with a deep, slow boing.
clips.note: Guitar: Emilyguitar by Karoryfer (CC0). Played in code.

clips.title: The rough end
clips.caption: VALVE with DRIVE up. One call of a sound-system siren, a beep then two notes flipping, tips the tank into its howl. DECAY eases down from 9 seconds and the howl settles into a long tail.
clips.transcript: A sound-system siren, a single beep followed by a high and a low note flipping quickly back and forth, once. The springs catch it and keep going on their own as a rough, moving roar. From nine seconds the roar slowly loosens over several seconds, then rings out as a long tail.
